text: Veltrazine is indicated for the treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults.
The most common adverse reactions (incidence of 5% or more) are headache, nausea, and upper respiratory tract infection. Serious infections, including tuberculosis, have been reported.
Screen patients for latent tuberculosis before starting Veltrazine. Do not administer live vaccines during treatment.
The recommended dose of Veltrazine is 45 mg administered subcutaneously at Week 0 and Week 4, then every 12 weeks thereafter.
Norimex is indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Common adverse reactions include diarrhea, nausea, and abdominal discomfort. Lactic acidosis is a rare but serious complication.
Norimex is contraindicated in patients with severe renal impairment (eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2) and in patients with metabolic acidosis.
Start Norimex at 500 mg orally twice daily with meals. The dose may be increased in increments of 500 mg weekly to a maximum of 2000 mg per day.
Cardiolan is indicated to reduce the risk of stroke in patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation.

Cardiolan increases the risk of bleeding, which can be serious and fatal. Premature discontinuation increases the risk of thrombotic events. Spinal or epidural hematoma may occur in patients receiving neuraxial anesthesia.
The recommended dose of Cardiolan is 20 mg once daily with the evening meal. In patients with creatinine clearance 15 to 50 mL/min the recommended dose is 15 mg once daily.
Somnirol is indicated for the short-term treatment of insomnia characterized by difficulty with sleep onset.

Complex sleep behaviors, including sleep-walking, sleep-driving, and engaging in other activities while not fully awake, may occur after taking Somnirol. Discontinue immediately if a patient experiences a complex sleep behavior.
Available data on Somnirol use in pregnant women are insufficient to evaluate for a drug-associated risk of major birth defects or miscarriage.
